> ⭐ **`STACK-§2`'s *"a non-uniform scale preserves ⛔ nothing"* is ⛔ MEASURED FALSE for the standoff, ⛔ in the GOOD direction — it ⛔ IMPROVES: `103.32 → 112.38 → 115.10 → 116.40 → 117.15`, ⛔ clearing `≥ 98.0` at ⛔ ALL FIVE `n`.**
> ⛔ **The tower ⛔ still stops at ⛔ ×2, and ⛔ not for any reason ⛔ anyone had written down.**

**1. ⛔⛔ THE ARITHMETIC THAT SETS THE CEILING — ⛔ WRITTEN OUT, ⛔ BECAUSE IT IS ⛔ CHECKABLE AND ⛔ NOBODY SHOULD HAVE TO RE-DERIVE IT.**

`FSiegeLadderClimbStatics::Begin` sizes the ⛔ non-swept deck-breach window as `DeckBreachCapsuleHalfHeights (3) × HalfHeight` — a property of the ⛔ **PAWN**, ⛔ invariant in `n`. The deck slab (`UCX_SM_WatchTower_07`, `Z [1160, 1200]`) is a property of the ⛔ **MESH** ⇒ ⛔ **`40 n` uu thick.**

```
window OPENS at capsule-centre Z  =  1200n − 2·HH
sweep  JAMS  at capsule-centre Z  =  1160n − HH      (capsule TOP meets the slab underside)

need OPEN <= JAM  :  1200n − 2·HH <= 1160n − HH   <=>   40n <= HH   <=>   n <= HH / 40
     unit HH = 88  ->  n <= 2.2   (⛔ BINDING)        hero HH = 96  ->  n <= 2.4
```

- ⛔⛔ **THE ⛔ AI UNIT BINDS, ⛔ NOT THE HERO** — ⭐ **which ⛔ INVERTS `TOWER-§8.5a`'s standing intuition that the hero's ⛔ FATTER capsule is the hazard. ⛔ Here the hero's ⛔ TALLER capsule buys it ⛔ MORE window.**
- ⭐⭐ **AND THE HEADROOM WAS ⛔ ALREADY DECLARED, ⛔ IN THE SOURCE, ⛔ BY THE CONSTANT ITSELF:** `DeckBreachCapsuleHalfHeights`' own doc comment says it is *"⛔ **2.2× the ~40 uu the mesh actually ships**"*. ⇒ ⚖️ ***⛔ A Z STACK SPENDS EXACTLY THAT HEADROOM, ⛔ LINEARLY IN `n`. ⛔ The margin was ⛔ documented and ⛔ nobody had connected it to ⛔ scaling.***

| `n` | slab | window opens @ `Zc` | sweep jams @ `Zc` | margin | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 40 | 1024 | 1072 | **+48.00** | ✅ ships today |
| **2** | **80** | 2224 | 2232 | ⭐ **+8.00** | ✅ **PASS — the licensed ceiling** |
| 3 | 120 | 3424 | 3392 | ⛔ **−32.00** | ⛔ watchdog drop |
| 4 | 160 | 4624 | 4552 | ⛔ **−72.00** | ⛔ watchdog drop |
| 5 | 200 | 5824 | 5712 | ⛔ **−112.00** | ⛔ watchdog drop |

⛔ **WHAT `n ≥ 3` IS IN PLAY: the swept capsule's top meets the slab underside ⛔ BEFORE `ShouldSweep` turns sweeping off. It cannot advance, the window ⛔ never opens, and the climber hangs in `MOVE_Flying` until `§8.5a` cl. 7's watchdog ⛔ drops it from ~3,392 uu.** ⭐ **The one good thing: cl. 7 makes that failure ⛔ LOUD, ⛔ not silent.** ⛔ **It is still a tower whose deck ⛔ cannot be reached — ⛔ exactly the `STACK-§8` cl. 2 outcome the ban existed to prevent.**

**2. ⚖️⛔⛔ THE RULING, AND ⛔ HOW IT MUST BE DESCRIBED — ⛔ SHIP AT ×2, AND ⛔ RECORD THE SHORTFALL PLAINLY.**

- ⚖️ **DEFAULT (⛔ proceeding unless 🧑 Jonathan rules otherwise): ⛔ SHIP AT ×2.** ⭐ **`MaxStackHeightMultiplier` per class is ⛔ already the shape `STACK-§8` cl. 4 + `J-13` chose, so the partial costs ⛔ no new machinery, and `J-6`'s cap behaviour ⛔ already paints the ghost ⛔ BLUE at the ceiling with ⛔ zero new UI.** ⚖️ *⛔ A ⛔ MEASURED ×2 that ⛔ ships beats a ⛔ THEORISED ×5 that ⛔ voids the climb.*
- ⛔⛔ **AND THE HONEST SENTENCE, ⛔ WHICH IS ⛔ NOT OPTIONAL: 🧑 HIS SPEC SAID ⛔ ×2 → ×5. ⛔ THIS IS A ⛔ MEASURED SHORTFALL AGAINST IT, ⛔ NOT A DESIGN CHOICE, AND ⛔ NO ROW, HANDOFF, COMMIT MESSAGE OR SLACK POST MAY DRESS IT AS ONE.** ⛔ **The alternative — ⛔ HOLD the feature and ⛔ re-engineer the deck window to scale — was ⛔ put to him and is ⛔ his call, ⛔ not the board's.**
- ⛔ **`ArrowTower` and every other building are ⛔ UNAFFECTED and stay at ⛔ ×5** (`J-13`). ⛔ **The ceiling is ⛔ per class and ⛔ a second copy of it anywhere is a ⛔ FAIL.**
- ⛔ **IF the window is ever re-engineered to scale (⛔ i.e. `DeckBreachCapsuleHalfHeights` becomes a ⛔ slab-derived quantity rather than a pawn-derived one), ⛔ THIS CEILING IS ⛔ RE-DERIVED FROM THIS SECTION'S ARITHMETIC — ⛔ never bumped by hand.**

**3. ⭐ WHAT `n = 2` ACTUALLY BUYS — ⛔ MEASURED, ⛔ NOT HOPED.** A **2,400 uu** tower whose standoff is **+9.06 uu BETTER** than the one shipping today; whose ⛔ non-swept stretch **HALVES** (22.00 % → 11.00 % of the line, ⛔ i.e. ⛔ MORE of the ascent is swept ⇒ ⛔ strictly safer against `§8.5`'s named harms); whose foot and deck navmesh margins are **bit-identical at every `n`** (⛔ both are X/Y facts and a Z scale ⛔ cannot touch Y); and whose watchdog **scales with the line** (14.14 s → 27.64 s against a 6.91 s ascent) ⛔ because it was **derived, ⛔ never a literal**.

**4. ⛔ THE RUNG PLANE — ⛔ DEPTH SURVIVES · ⛔ PITCH IS ⛔ COSMETIC** (`STACK-§8` cl. 4's mandatory split, ⛔ discharged).

- ⭐ **DEPTH — the thing the hands ⛔ GRIP — ⛔ SURVIVES:** `22.000 → 22.502 → 22.599 → 22.633 → 22.649`, ⛔ **max +3.0 %**, closed form `depth(n) = 22n / sqrt(Ux² + n²Uz²)` ⛔ **bounded above by `22 / Uz = 22.677` at ⛔ ANY `n`.** ⇒ ⛔⛔ **`TOWER-§8.3`'s mesh↔clip binding does ⛔ NOT fire, and `A_SiegeBiped_Climb` needs ⛔ NO re-export on depth grounds. ⛔ No clip re-export is owed.**
- ⚠️ **PITCH ⛔ STRETCHES and is ⛔ COSMETIC:** `40 → 78.22 → 116.82 → 155.53 → 194.27`; ⛔ **rung COUNT unchanged (31)** and pitch-as-a-fraction-of-the-line ⛔ invariant. At `n = 2` the hands cycle at `4.47 Hz` against `8.75 Hz` of authored rung passage ⇒ ⛔ **hands grip between rungs about half the time.** ⛔ **This voids ⛔ NOTHING** (the depth is preserved, so the hands still land in the ladder slab) ⇒ ⛔ **it is a note for 🧑 Jonathan's eye, ⛔ NEVER a gate.** ⚖️ *⛔ Conflating pitch with depth is how a ⛔ shippable feature gets ⛔ refused.*

**5. ⚠️⚠️⛔ THE ⛔ NAV-LINK OCTREE HAZARD — ⛔ PREDICTED, ⛔ NOT MEASURED, AND IT IS ⛔ THE ONE THAT A ⛔ HERO-ONLY PLAYTEST ⛔ CANNOT SEE.**

- ✅ ⭐ **FIRST, THE HAZARD THAT WAS ⛔ REFUTED, ⛔ IN WRITING, SO IT IS ⛔ NOT RAISED AGAIN: ⛔ THE CLIMB LINE IS ⛔ NOT CACHED.** `ConfigureLadderLink()` has ⛔ exactly ⛔ ONE caller (`BeginPlay`) — ⛔ **but it stores a ⛔ RELATIVE transform.** `ResolveLadderSocketRelative` uses `RTS_Actor`, which ⛔ divides the actor transform (⛔ scale included) ⛔ straight back out; `NavLinkCustomComponent.cpp:518-525` ⛔ re-applies the ⛔ LIVE owner transform on ⛔ EVERY read. ⛔ **4 read sites, ⛔ ZERO caches** (⛔ negative control: the only `FVector` members on `AClimbableTower` are the two `static const` degrade-open fallbacks, ⛔ themselves relative). ⇒ ⛔ **a scaled tower does ⛔ NOT strand a climber at the old deck height.** ⭐ **`TOWER-§8.4(A)`'s `RTS_Actor` decision, made for the ⛔ spawn-squash, ⛔ pays for this for free.**
- ⚠️⚠️ **AND THE ⛔ ADJACENT ONE THAT IS ⛔ NOT REFUTED: ⛔ `UNavLinkCustomComponent` IS A `UActorComponent`, ⛔ NOT A `USceneComponent`.** ⇒ ⛔ **a root rescale runs `PropagateTransformUpdate` → `UpdateComponentInNavOctree` for the ⛔ SCENE component ⛔ only. ⛔ Nothing re-gathers the ⛔ LINK's octree element**, whose off-mesh connection was baked from the owner transform ⛔ at gather time. ⇒ ⛔ **the tower's ⛔ collision navmesh regenerates at the new height while the ⛔ registered connection may remain at the ⛔ old `Z = 1200`** ⇒ ⛔ **Recast can drop it and ⛔ AI UNITS STOP BEING HANDED A PATH TO THE LADDER.**
- ⛔⛔⭐ **THE PART THAT MAKES THIS LAW RATHER THAN A FOOTNOTE: ⛔ THE ⛔ HERO'S CONTACT CLIMB IS ⛔ UNAFFECTED — it reads `GetStartPoint()` ⛔ live and ⛔ never consults the navmesh.** ⇒ ⚖️ ***⛔ A HERO-ONLY PLAYTEST WOULD ⛔ PASS WHILE THE BOT'S UNITS ⛔ SILENTLY FAIL TO PATH UP. ⛔ That sentence goes on the ⛔ acceptance row ⛔ in those words, ⛔ every time side (iii) is discharged.***
- ✅ **CHEAP TO CLOSE, ⛔ AND THE CLOSURE IS ⛔ MANDATORY ON ANY ROW THAT APPLIES A RUNTIME SCALE: ⛔ re-call `ConfigureLadderLink()` ⛔ after a successful `ApplyStackUpgrade`** — it re-reads the ⛔ same scale-free relatives and drives `SetLinkData` → `UpdateNavigationBounds` + `RefreshNavigationModifiers`. ⛔ **Guard it with a ⛔ CALL-SHAPE test (`SC-§41`), ⛔ not a bare token.**

**6. ⚠️ TWO ⛔ LATENT TRAPS RECORDED BESIDE THE FEATURE — ⛔ NEITHER IS A DEFECT TODAY, ⛔ BOTH ARE ONE EDIT AWAY.**

- ⚠️⛔ **(a) `USiegeMeshJuiceComponent` CAN ⛔ SILENTLY UN-STACK A TOWER.** `SetTargetMesh` snapshots `BaseScale` and the squash's terminal branch writes `SetRelativeScale3D(BaseScale)` ⛔ verbatim. ⭐ **Measured ⛔ SAFE as shipped** (one call, at `ABuilding::BeginPlay`; the channel runs only while `bSquashActive`; `AClimbableTower : public ABuilding`, ⛔ not `ATower`, so `PlayRecoil` can never reach it). ⛔ **THE TRAP: ⛔ a stack upgrade is ⛔ exactly the moment someone would want a squash** ⇒ ⛔ **any future `PlaySpawnSquash()` on a stacked building ⛔ resets the mesh to the ×1 baseline and ⛔ UN-STACKS the tower — height ⛔ and climb line together — with ⛔ every readback correct.** ⇒ ⛔ **a comment naming this trap sits ⛔ beside `ApplyStackUpgrade`.**
- ⚠️ **(b) `AClimbableTower::PlatformHeightUU = 1200.f` becomes a ⛔ LIE at `n > 1`.** ⛔ **Measured harmless today: ⛔ ZERO non-test consumers of `GetPlatformHeightUU`** (⛔ 3 references, ⛔ all in `Tests/SiegeClimbableTowerTest.cpp`, ⛔ reading the ⛔ CDO, which a runtime instance scale cannot touch). ⛔ **It becomes a defect the moment a `HIGH-§` consumer binds to it.**

## ⚖️ THE WITCH + INVISIBILITY (2026-09-03) — namespace **`WITCH-§`**

📌 **BORN WITH ITS NAMESPACE PREFIX (`WITCH-§N`).** Cite as `WITCH-§3`, ⛔ never a bare `§3`.
📌 **Jonathan's directive is the specification and lives HERE, verbatim, ⛔ once. ⛔ No task below restates it:**

> *"The first card is a unit that spawns, This unit is called a 'witch' and is able to walk up to nearby units and make them invisible. Here is how an invisible units works: Invisible units are completely invisible to enemy AI and enemy players. From your perspective, they are simply slightly transparent/translucent, meaning that instead of seeing them as their normal colors will be a much lighter color that you can see through, and the objects you see through them are going to be blurred, giving that translucent effect. Invisible units will remain invisble until they attack/heal/mine/power up something (basically if they do anything other than walk), to which then they permanently go back to visible(unless they are later made invisible by a witch again). The witch costs 50 gold, is controllable by all commands, and will always cast the invisible spell on the nearest visible unit that is within their position circle, however unlike the cleric and sorcerer spells which are instant, this spell has a an animation that lasts 3 seconds, which can be interupted if the witch or unit that is turning invisible are attacked. The witch can only make one unit at a time invisible."*

### WITCH-§0 ⭐⭐⭐ **THE HEADLINE — ⛔ INVISIBILITY CANNOT RIDE THE GHOST'S SEAM, AND THE REASON IS ⛔ STRUCTURAL, ⛔ NOT A PREFERENCE**

⚠️ **The ghost is the obvious precedent and it is the ⛔ RIGHT place to look — but ⛔ it does ⛔ not transfer, and shipping it as if it did would ship an ⛔ INVULNERABLE unit.**

- ✅ **WHAT IS TRUE AND MEASURED (re-verified at source 2026-09-03, ⛔ not taken from `GHOST-§1` on faith):** every hostile-actor selection in this project enumerates its candidate universe with `UGameplayStatics::GetAllActorsWithInterface(World, UTeamAgent::StaticClass(), …)`. ⭐ **Nine live call sites, each read:** `SummonedUnit.cpp:1663` · `SummonedUnit.cpp:2208` · `Tower.cpp:220` · `Tower.cpp:378` · `SiegeCombatStatics.cpp:36` (⭐ **`ApplyRadialDamage` — EVERY AoE**) · `SpellLibrary.cpp:64` · `SpellLineSweep.cpp:133` · `HeroCharacter.cpp:551` · `SiegeCheatManager.cpp:130` (⛔ the cheat lane, ⛔ which is ⛔ not a combat path but ⛔ is a site).
- ⛔⛔ **AND HERE IS WHY THE GHOST'S ANSWER IS ⛔ UNAVAILABLE.** `ASiegeGhostPawn` is untargetable because it ⛔ **does not implement `ITeamAgent` at all**. ⚠️ **That is a ⛔ COMPILE-TIME, ⛔ CLASS-LEVEL, ⛔ PERMANENT property.** Invisibility is ⛔ **per-instance**, ⛔ **runtime**, ⛔ **reversible**, and — ⭐ **by his own sentence** — ⛔ **must preserve ATTACKABILITY**: *"can be interupted if the witch or unit that is turning invisible are attacked."*
- ⇒ ⛔⛔ **AN INVISIBLE UNIT THAT LEFT `ITeamAgent` WOULD BE UNATTACKABLE, WHICH WOULD MAKE HIS OWN INTERRUPTION RULE ⛔ UNREACHABLE AND THE CARD ⛔ UNCOUNTERABLE.** ⭐ **The ghost's mechanism and this feature's requirement are ⛔ in direct opposition. ⛔ Do not let the resemblance carry.**
- ⚖️ **AND THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS THE REAL RISK:** invisibility ⛔ **must** therefore be a **flag consulted at a guard point** — ⭐ **which is ⛔ EXACTLY the design `GHOST-§1` REFUSED**, in writing, for a stated reason (*"a flag can be forgotten at a guard point; an actor that is not in the candidate list cannot be…"*). ⛔ **We are knowingly adopting the weaker pattern because the requirement forbids the stronger one.** ⇒ ⭐ **the mitigation is `WITCH-§1` and it is ⛔ NOT optional.**

### WITCH-§1 ⛔⛔ **THE MITIGATION IS A ***FUNNEL***: ⛔ NINE HAND-EDITED GUARDS ARE AN AUTOMATIC FAIL**

- ⛔⛔ **MEASURED: THERE IS ⛔ NO SHARED CHOKEPOINT TODAY.** Each of the nine sites enumerates, then ⛔ **independently** does `Cast<ITeamAgent>` → `GetTeamId() == Team` → its own distance test. ⚠️ **`SiegeCombatStatics.cpp:38-51` is the pattern; ⛔ every other site re-implements it.**
- ✅ **THE LAW: ⛔ ONE new gatherer, and ⛔ all nine sites route through it.** **`FSiegeCombatStatics::GatherHostileAgents(const UWorld* World, ETeamId ViewerTeam, TArray<AActor*>& Out)`** — ⛔ **the ⛔ ONLY place `GetAllActorsWithInterface(UTeamAgent…)` may appear after this batch.**
- ⛔⛔⛔ **CORRECTED 2026-09-03 — ⛔ THE SIGNATURE ABOVE ORIGINALLY PINNED `ESiegeTeam`, WHICH ⛔ DOES NOT EXIST. ⭐ THE SHIPPED ENUM IS `ETeamId` (`TeamId.h:14`).** ⚠️ **Measured by `TASK-837` while reading the funnel it does ⛔ not own; ⛔ zero hits for `ESiegeTeam` anywhere in `Source/`.** ⇒ 📌 **NEW LAW, ⛔ general, ⛔ not fog-specific: ⛔ A SYMBOL WRITTEN INTO A SPEC IS AN ⛔ INSTRUCTION, ⛔ NOT A DESCRIPTION — ⭐ an agent handed `ESiegeTeam` ⛔ invents the type rather than doubting the manager.** ⚖️ *Same family as `SC-§37` (a test transcribed from its spec cannot fail) and `§23`'s base-of-a-measurement: ⛔ the error is ⛔ not that a name was wrong, it is that the ⛔ wrong name was ⛔ authoritative.* ✅ **⇒ every type/function/asset name a task row pins must be ⛔ read out of the tree before the row is written, and ⛔ a phantom found downstream is a ⛔ CONVENTIONS correction, ⛔ never a silent per-task substitution.**
- ⭐ **A grep for `GetAllActorsWithInterface` returning more than ⛔ ONE `Source/` hit (plus the cheat lane, ⛔ explicitly exempted and ⛔ named) is a ⛔ QA BLOCKER.** ⚖️ *This is the `VIS-§1` leaf-grep idiom used as a ⛔ gate rather than a ⛔ report.*
- ⛔ **THE FUNNEL IS ITS OWN TASK AND IT IS ⛔ BEHAVIOUR-NEUTRAL.** It lands, compiles and passes the ⛔ existing suite with ⛔ **zero** invisibility in it. ⭐ **Only then does the flag get consulted inside it.** ⚠️ **A refactor and a feature in one commit is how a regression becomes unattributable.**

### WITCH-§2 ⚖️ **"COMPLETELY INVISIBLE TO ENEMY AI" — THE FOUR LANES, RULED SEPARATELY BECAUSE THEY ARE ⛔ NOT ONE THING**

| lane | ruling | why |
|---|---|---|
| **enemy unit/tower/hero ACQUISITION** (7 of the 9 sites) | ✅ **SUPPRESSED — an invisible unit is ⛔ not returned to an ⛔ enemy-team viewer** | ⭐ this ⛔ is the feature |
| ⛔ **AoE / `ApplyRadialDamage`** | ⛔⛔ **NOT SUPPRESSED — an invisible unit ⛔ IS caught by a blast** | ⚖️ **a blast is ⛔ not an act of seeing.** ⭐ It also gives the card a ⛔ real counter (Fireball/Sapper/BombTower flush a veiled push) ⇒ ⛔ the 50-gold card is ⛔ not an auto-win. 🧑 **`J-W2` — reversible on one word** |

| ⛔ **FRIENDLY acquisition + the OWNER's own orders** | ⛔⛔ **NEVER SUPPRESSED** | ⛔ **An invisible unit that its own player cannot select, order or heal is a ⛔ BUG, ⛔ not a feature.** The suppression predicate takes the ⛔ VIEWER'S TEAM and is ⛔ inert for allies |

## ⚖️ THE FOG CARD (2026-09-03) — namespace **`FOG-§`**

📌 **Jonathan's directive, verbatim, ⛔ once:**

> *"The second card is a 'fog' card. It costs 50 gold and will roll a fog into the map. The fog makes it to where players can really only see up until about 20 feet in front of you. ### FOG-§1 ⭐⛔⛔ **THE UNIT CONVERSION — PINNED ONCE, WITH THE ARITHMETIC SHOWN, SO ⛔ NOBODY RE-DERIVES IT**

> ### **1 ft = 30.48 cm (exact, by international definition).**
> ### **10 ft = 10 × 30.48 = 304.8 cm = ⭐ `304.8 uu`**
> ### **20 ft = 20 × 30.48 = 609.6 cm = ⭐ `609.6 uu`**

- ⛔⛔ **`304.8` AND `609.6` ARE THE ONLY NUMBERS. ⛔ NOT 300/600 ("close enough"), ⛔ NOT 10/20 (feet-as-units).** ⚠️ **Feet-as-units is wrong by ⛔ 30× and ⛔ looks entirely plausible in review** — a `20` in a float named `FogVisibilityUU` reads fine and would put the fog ceiling ⛔ *inside the unit's own capsule*.
- ✅ **They ship as ⛔ TWO named `EditDefaultsOnly` constants carrying the arithmetic in their comments** — **`FogVisionCeilingUU = 609.6f`** and **`FogVisionOnsetUU = 304.8f`** — and ⛔ **no second literal of either exists anywhere in the codebase.**
- ⭐ **THIS IS THE SAME LAW AS `HIGH-§1`'s `152.4`, AND IT IS THE SECOND TIME HE HAS SPECIFIED A DISTANCE IN FEET.** ⇒ ⛔ **feet-in-prose is now a ⛔ recognised project idiom: any future number he gives in feet is converted ⛔ at 30.48 and ⛔ pinned with its arithmetic.**

### FOG-§7a ⭐ **THE FALLOFF SHIPPED AS ⛔ QUADRATIC EASE-IN (`t²`), ⛔ NOT LINEAR — ⛔ downstream specs that assumed linear are ⛔ WRONG** (`TASK-837`, ruled + shipped)

- ✅ **`density(d)` on `[0,1]`: ⛔ `0` at/inside `FogVisionOnsetUU` → `t^FogDensityExponent` where `t = (d − onset)/(ceiling − onset)` → ⛔ `1` at/beyond `FogVisionCeilingUU`.** ⭐ **`FogDensityExponent = 2.f` ships as a ⛔ THIRD `EditDefaultsOnly` tunable** — ⛔ a ⛔ shape, ⛔ not a distance, so it ⛔ cannot carry `FOG-§1`'s 30× trap. *"Make it linear"* is a one-word retune to `1.0`.
- ⭐ **WHY (both halves of his sentence, ⛔ and they both point ⛔ away from linear):** *"a ⛔ **light** amount of fog ⛔ **starting** at about 10 feet"* — an ease-in leaves the onset with ⛔ zero slope; ⛔ **one uu past the onset, quadratic reads `0.0000108` and ⛔ linear reads `0.0033` — ⛔ 300× more, i.e. a ⛔ visible EDGE exactly where he asked for a haze.** And *"it gets ⛔ **thicker and thicker**"* is an ⛔ acceleration, ⛔ not a constant rate (quadratic gains ⛔ 0.25 over the first half of the band and ⛔ 0.75 over the second).
- ⛔ **NOT smoothstep** (eases ⛔ out, flattening at the ⛔ one place his sentence is absolute) · ⛔ **NOT Beer-Lambert** (⛔ concave — ⛔ the exact opposite of "thicker and thicker" — ⛔ and asymptotic, so it ⛔ can never reach the state he named).
- ✅ **THE CEILING IS A ⛔ HARD CUT, ⛔ not an asymptote.** *"really cannot see ⛔ **anything** beyond 20 feet"* is absolute; ⛔ an asymptote reading `0.97` leaves ⛔ 3% visibility, and ⛔ at Longbowman range 3% is a ⛔ lethal shot. ⭐ A hard cut is also the ⛔ only version that is ⛔ assertable exactly.
- ✅ **ACQUISITION ONLY — ⛔ an arrow already in the air ⛔ still lands.** His words cover the decision to ⛔ *fire*. ⭐ Same shipped precedent as `WITCH-§2`'s target-locked projectiles (`Projectile.cpp:352`). ⛔ **Declared residual: a volley fired the instant before fog lands ⛔ still connects** — exposure is ⛔ tiny, because firing is ⛔ already clamped.
- ⛔⛔ **SYMMETRY (`J-F3`) IS ENFORCED ⛔ STRUCTURALLY, ⛔ NOT BY A RUNTIME CHECK: ⛔ NOT ONE FUNCTION IN `SiegeFogStatics` TAKES A TEAM, A VIEWER, A CONTROLLER OR AN ACTOR.** ⇒ ⭐ **an asymmetric fog is ⛔ UNREPRESENTABLE — ⛔ you cannot write the favouritism because there is ⛔ no parameter to branch on.** ⇒ ⛔⛔ **DO ⛔ NOT ADD A TEAM PARAMETER TO "SUPPORT" SYMMETRY, and ⛔ DO ⛔ NOT WRITE A *"both teams get the same answer"* TEST — ⭐ it would be ⛔ trivially true and would report ⛔ SAFE forever.** ⚖️ *Note the ⛔ deliberate contrast with `WITCH-§`: the ⛔ invisibility predicate ⛔ DOES take viewer + target team, ⛔ because that feature ⛔ IS asymmetric. ⭐ **The two signatures ⛔ disagree on purpose, and ⛔ that disagreement is the design.***
- ⚠️ **THE BOUNDARY, ⛔ DELIBERATE AND ⛔ NOT A BUG:** at `d == 609.6` ⛔ exactly, `FogDensityAt` returns ⛔ `1.0` (opaque) while `IsVisibleThroughFog` returns ⛔ **true** (still in range). ⭐ The project's shipped acquisition idiom is ⛔ **inclusive** (`SummonedUnit.cpp:1644`, `:1785`, `:1851`, `:1956`, `:2409` — all `<= AttackRange`) ⇒ ⛔ **the clamp substitutes the ⛔ OPERAND of that comparison, ⛔ never its SHAPE.** ⛔ Two different consumers asking different questions at ⛔ one float of measure zero.
- ✅ **AND THE PROPERTY THAT MAKES THE WHOLE THING SAFE TO CALL UNCONDITIONALLY: `EffectiveVisionRadius` returns `RequestedRadiusUU` ⛔ BIT-IDENTICALLY when `bFogActive == false`** — ⛔ no clamp, ⛔ no sanitising, ⛔ not one ulp of drift. ⇒ ⭐ **with fog off the game is ⛔ byte-for-byte the game that shipped, which is ⛔ what keeps any fog regression ⛔ ATTRIBUTABLE TO FOG.**
- ✅⭐⭐ **THE DISAGREEMENT ⛔ SURVIVED AN ⛔ ADVERSARIAL READING — ⛔ MEASURED 2026-09-03 BY `TASK-847`, ⛔ WHICH IS THE ⛔ ONLY REASON THIS BULLET IS WORTH MORE THAN THE ONE ABOVE IT.** ⛔ **The two modules were put under ⛔ ONE pair of eyes ⛔ precisely to catch either acquiring the other's shape, and ⛔ neither did: ⛔ NO team/viewer/controller/actor parameter reached ⛔ any fog function · ⛔ NO distance or time term reached ⛔ any of invisibility's six signatures · ⛔ NEITHER header includes the other · ⛔ and the phantom `ESiegeTeam` returns ⛔ ZERO hits across ⛔ ALL of `Source/` (the shipped enum is `ETeamId`).** ⇒ ⭐ **`FOG-§7a`'s *"the two signatures disagree on purpose"* and `WITCH-§1`'s reason for existing are now true of the ⛔ SHIPPED CODE, ⛔ not merely of the law.** ⚖️ *⛔ A law that has ⛔ survived a real gate is worth more than one that has only been ⛔ written — ⭐ and a ⛔ structural guarantee is the ⛔ only kind that can be ⛔ measured this way at all.*

### FOG-§7b ⚖️⛔⛔⛔ **`FogVisionCeilingUU == 0` BLINDS THE ENTIRE ARMY — AND IT SITS ON THE TUNABLE'S ⛔ OWN SLIDER STOP. ⛔ RULED, ⛔ NOT LEFT IMPLICIT.** (added 2026-09-03, from `TASK-847` WARN-3)

#### ⚖️⛔⛔⭐⭐ **FOG-§10.7 — THE 2026-09-04 `BrightSun` RULINGS: ⛔ THE DATUM · ⛔ THE SAMPLE · ⛔ FOG-ON-FOG · ⛔ SUN-ON-SUN. ⛔ FOUR CLOSED IN ⛔ ONE MESSAGE.**

> 📌 **HIS WORDS, VERBATIM:** *"that message I just gave about bright sun still being up is ⛔ only for when the 'fog' card gets played. If bright sun is played during the bright sun window, then the timer gets ⛔ reset to whatever the new time would be under the new cast, ⛔ unless that new time would be ⛔ less than the current time, then the player will just get a message that says '⛔ using bright sun right now would reduce fog prevention time from "x" time to "y" time' where 'x' is the ⛔ current time left and 'y' is the ⛔ new fog prevention time under the current height calculation, and the player is ⛔ basically prevented from playing the card. If ⛔ fog is played during fog then the timer is ⛔ reset to 5 minutes. For calculating 'bright sun' fog prevention time, the height is ⛔ sampled at the time that the card is cast. The ground is simply the elevation of the ⛔ flat grass terrain, ⛔ not including the hills, therefore that ground height number should be the ⛔ same anywhere on the map, and it should be the ⛔ same height in which ranged units' damage is at ⛔ 1 times their damage and increases by 10% every ⛔ 5 feet above that."*

##### ⛔⛔⭐⭐ **(A) `J-F18` — SUN-ON-SUN IS ⛔ CONDITIONAL. ⛔ NOT `max`, ⛔ NOT refresh, ⛔ NOT refuse — ⛔ A ⛔ BRANCH.**

| the new window vs the remaining one | ⛔ what happens |
|---|---|
| ⛔ **LONGER** | ⛔ **RESET to the new duration.** ⛔ Gold spent, ⛔ card consumed, ⛔ normal cast |
| ⛔ **SHORTER** (⛔ or equal — ⛔ see the boundary note) | ⛔⛔ **REFUSED. ⛔ NO GOLD SPENT · ⛔ CARD ⛔ NOT CONSUMED · ⛔ message: *"using bright sun right now would reduce fog prevention time from X to Y"*** |

- ⭐⭐ **THE OLD DEFAULT WAS ⛔ RIGHT ABOUT THE ⛔ DURATION AND ⛔ WRONG ABOUT THE ⛔ COST, AND THAT IS THE ⛔ WHOLE DELTA.** ⛔ `max(remaining, new)` and *"reset if longer"* produce the ⛔ IDENTICAL remaining time in the ⛔ longer case. ⇒ ⛔ **they diverge ⛔ ONLY in the ⛔ shorter case, where `max` would have ⛔ silently kept the timer while ⛔ BILLING the player 60 gold and ⛔ EATING the card.** ⚖️ ***The default's ⛔ arithmetic was correct and its ⛔ economics were not — and ⛔ no test of the resulting duration could ever have caught that.***
- ⛔⛔ **THIS IS THE ⛔ SAME THREE-PROPERTY SHAPE AS `J-F19` (`FOG-§10.6`): ⛔ no gold · ⛔ card retained · ⛔ a message carrying ⛔ LIVE values.** ⇒ ⛔ **the two refusals are ⛔ SIBLINGS and ⛔ share their machinery.**
- ⛔ **BUT THEY ⛔ DIFFER IN ⛔ ARITY, AND THAT DECIDES ⛔ WHAT IS ACTUALLY SHARED:** `J-F19`'s message carries ⛔ **ONE** value; `J-F18`'s carries ⛔ **TWO**. ⇒ ⛔⛔ **THE SHARED THING IS THE ⛔ SECONDS→`FText` FORMATTER (⛔ one scalar in, ⛔ one `FText` out), ⛔ CALLED ⛔ ONCE BY ONE MESSAGE AND ⛔ TWICE BY THE OTHER. ⛔ IT IS ⛔ NOT A SHARED MESSAGE BUILDER — ⛔ a builder cannot span two arities and an attempt to make it will produce an optional-second-value parameter that is ⛔ dead half the time.**
- ⛔⛔⭐⭐ **THE MECHANISM CONSEQUENCE THAT IS ⛔ EASY TO MISS AND IS A ⛔ SEAM REQUIREMENT, ⛔ NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL: ⛔ `Y` IS *"the new fog prevention time ⛔ UNDER THE CURRENT HEIGHT CALCULATION"* ⇒ ⛔ THE REFUSAL MUST ⛔ COMPUTE A ⛔ FULL `BrightSun` DURATION ⛔ JUST TO EXPLAIN WHY IT REFUSES.** ⇒ ⛔ **THE DURATION CALCULATION MUST BE ⛔ CALLABLE ⛔ OUTSIDE THE CAST PATH.** ⛔ **A duration computed ⛔ inside `ApplyBrightSun` (or ⛔ inline in the cast branch) ⛔ cannot be reached by the refusal ⛔ without either ⛔ duplicating the formula or ⛔ casting the card to find out whether to cast it.** ⭐ **Both of those are ⛔ defects; ⛔ the seam is the ⛔ fix, and it must be ⛔ boarded as a ⛔ REQUIREMENT.**
- ⛔ **AND `Y` DEPENDS ON HERO POSITION ⛔ AT THAT INSTANT** ⇒ ⛔ **BOTH values are ⛔ LIVE. ⛔ `X` is the live remainder (⛔ `FOG-§10.6`'s law, ⛔ unchanged); ⛔ `Y` is a live height sample.** ⛔ **Neither may be cached at cast time.**
- ⚠️ **THE ⛔ EQUAL BOUNDARY IS A ⛔ DECLARED DEFAULT, ⛔ NOT HIS WORD: he wrote *"⛔ unless that new time would be ⛔ LESS than the current time"*.** ⇒ ⛔ **EQUAL is ⛔ not "less" ⇒ ⛔ EQUAL ⛔ RESETS (i.e. it is a ⛔ legal, ⛔ if pointless, cast).** ⛔ **Ship the ⛔ strict `new < remaining ⇒ refuse` reading — ⛔ it is the ⛔ literal one — and ⛔ note that a float-equal window is ⛔ unreachable in practice.**

##### ✅ **(B) `J-F15` — SAMPLED ⛔ AT CAST TIME. ⛔ THE DEFAULT WAS RIGHT; ⛔ NOTHING UNWINDS.**
##### ✅ **(C) `J-F16` — FOG ON FOG ⇒ ⛔ RESET TO `300` s. ⛔ THE DEFAULT WAS RIGHT; ⛔ NOTHING UNWINDS.** ⭐ **His sentence ⛔ independently re-derives `FogDurationSeconds == 300.f` — ⛔ the same number from ⛔ two different sentences of his, ⛔ which is the ⛔ strongest confirmation a tunable ever gets here.**

##### ⛔⛔⛔⭐⭐ **(D) `J-F13` — THE DATUM. ⛔ ONE CONSTANT, ⛔ TWO CONSUMERS — AND THE ⛔ MEASUREMENT SAYS THE SECOND CONSUMER ⛔ DOES NOT EXIST YET.**

> ⚖️ **HIS RULING JOINS TWO NUMBERS THAT WERE NEVER JOINED:** *"that ground height number should be the ⛔ same anywhere on the map, and it should be the ⛔ SAME HEIGHT IN WHICH RANGED UNITS' DAMAGE IS AT ⛔ 1 TIMES THEIR DAMAGE."*

- ⛔ **(d) THE CONTRACT IS THE ⛔ SHIPPED `USettingsMenuWidget` CONTRACT, ⛔ CLONED:** `BindWidgetOptional` members · `BlueprintCallable` wrappers · ⛔ `FString`/`int32`/`bool`-only `BlueprintImplementableEvent` params. ⛔ **NEVER an enum, ⛔ never a struct, in a BIE parameter.**
- ⛔ **(e) ⛔ VERIFICATION IS A ⛔ PIXEL / ⛔ HUMAN CHECK.** ⛔ There is ⛔ no `.uasset` to read back, and ⛔ MCP readback has ⛔ repeatedly passed on ⛔ visually-broken UMG here (⛔ `TASK-355`: ⛔ 6/6 bindings correct while ⛔ stacked in a ⛔ 165×48 px box in the corner — ⛔ a binding readback ⛔ cannot see geometry).
- ⛔ **(f) ⛔ NEW, AND ⛔ THIS LANE'S OWN: the ⛔ BACKDROP IS ⛔ HIT-TEST ⛔ VISIBLE.** ⛔ The panel sits ⛔ ON TOP of the ⛔ live settings panel, which is ⛔ on top of the ⛔ live main menu, and ⛔ neither is removed. ⛔ A `HIT_TEST_INVISIBLE` plate would ship a ⛔ live click-through into ⛔ Play / Sandbox / Deck Builder / ⛔ QUIT ⛔ while the panel looks modal. ⛔ **QA criterion: with Graphics open, a backdrop click reaches ⛔ NOTHING behind it.** ⛔ `Back` calls `RemoveFromParent()` on ⛔ THIS widget and ⛔ nothing else.

- ⛔ **THE ⛔ ONE EXCEPTION, ⛔ NAMED: the ⛔ FPS-counter ⛔ preference (`GFX-§7`) is a ⛔ UI preference, ⛔ not hardware ⇒ it ⛔ DOES belong in the ⛔ existing profile-scoped `USiegeSettingsSaveGame`, ⛔ added by the ⛔ "HOW TO ADD SETTING #2" recipe ~~(⛔ FOUR steps)~~ ⛔ **— ⛔ WHICH IS A ⛔ FIVE-STEP RECIPE —** already written in `SiegeSettingsSubsystem.h:70-80` (⛔ the five steps) ⛔ + `:82-94` (⛔ why step 5 exists).**

A — ⛔ **WRONG WHILE APPEARING CORRECT**).

### `GFX-§5` — ⚖️ **RULING 3: ⛔ A SLIDER WHERE A SLIDER IS ⛔ HONEST. ⛔ NEVER FAKE CONTINUITY OVER 5 STATES.**

🧑 **He said *"sliders"*, and he gets sliders — ⛔ but a control that ⛔ glides through 5 discrete states is ⛔ lying about what it does.**

| Control | Widget | Why |
|---|---|---|
| ⛔ the ⛔ 10 quality groups | ⛔ `USlider`, ⛔ `StepSize 0.25` ⇒ ⛔ **5 detents**, ⛔ live level name ⛔ beside it | ⛔ **it ⛔ IS a slider — ⛔ it simply ⛔ cannot land between detents, and ⛔ the label always states the ⛔ truth** |
| ⛔ Overall Quality preset | ⛔ same 5-detent slider, ⛔ + a read-only ⛔ **`Custom`** state | ⛔ shows `Custom` ⛔ when the groups ⛔ disagree — ⛔ never a ⛔ silent lie about the preset |
| ⛔ **Resolution Scale** | ⛔ **genuinely continuous** slider, ⛔ 50–100%, ⛔ 1% steps | ⛔ the ⛔ one control that ⛔ really is continuous — ⛔ and the ⛔ single ⛔ biggest perf lever |
| ⛔ Frame Rate Limit | ⛔ **stepper** over ⛔ 30/60/90/120/144/165/240/⛔ Unlimited | ⛔ a slider would ⛔ misrepresent the ⛔ spacing between those values |
| ⛔ Screen Resolution · Window Mode | ⛔ **stepper/combo** | ⛔ ⛔ unordered sets. ⛔ **NEVER a slider.** |
| ⛔ VSync · FPS counter | ⛔ **checkbox** | ⛔ boolean |

✅⭐ **CONFIRMED AT ENGINE SOURCE 2026-09-07 (⭐ `TASK-1112` §1.1) — ⛔ THIS TABLE NEEDED ⛔ NO CORRECTION:** ⛔ **every quality group is ⛔ `0..4` (`sg.<Group>.NumLevels` defaults to ⛔ `5`, `GetQualityLevelCounts()` `Scalability.cpp:1267-1283`) ⇒ ⛔ the ⛔ 5 detents (`StepSize 0.25`) are ⛔ RIGHT** · ⛔ **`Custom` is ⛔ ENGINE-NATIVE, ⛔ NOT ours to invent: `FQualityLevels::GetSingleQualityLevel()` (`Scalability.h:106`) is documented ⛔ `-1: custom` and backs `GetOverallScalabilityLevel()` (`GameUserSettings.cpp:971-974`).** ⇒ ⛔ **downstream rows use the ⛔ ENGINE'S OWN `-1` SENTINEL — ⛔ never a hand-rolled `bIsCustom` flag.** ⛔ **Level names likewise come from `Scalability::GetScalabilityNameFromQualityLevel(int32)` → `FText` (`Scalability.h:251`) — ⛔ the engine ⛔ already localises Low/Medium/High/Epic/Cinematic ⇒ ⛔ NO hand-written array.**

### 🚨⛔⛔⛔⭐⭐⭐ `GFX-§12` — **⛔ AN EFFECT THAT CHANGES WHAT A PLAYER CAN ⛔ SEE ⛔ FOR GAMEPLAY PURPOSES IS ⛔ NOT A SCALABILITY SETTING. ⛔ ITS ⛔ COST MAY SCALE; ⛔ ITS ⛔ PRESENCE MAY NOT.** (added 2026-09-08 by the manager, from 🧑 Jonathan's own reading of the shipped Shadows slider; ⛔ **it ⛔ CORRECTS `GFX-§9` and it ⛔ BINDS THE WHOLE GRAPHICS LANE FROM HERE ON**)

⛔⛔ **THE RULE, ⛔ STATED ONCE:** ⚖️ ***⛔ IF LOWERING A GRAPHICS SETTING CAN MAKE A PLAYER ⛔ BETTER AT THE GAME, THE SETTING IS ⛔ NOT A GRAPHICS SETTING — ⛔ IT IS A ⛔ CHEAT CODE WITH A ⛔ PERFORMANCE ALIBI.***

- ⛔ **⛔ THE TEST, ⛔ MECHANICAL, ⛔ SO IT IS ⛔ NOT A JUDGEMENT CALL: ⛔ for each option, ask ⛔ *"at the ⛔ LOWEST setting, does the player learn something the game ⛔ intended to hide, or ⛔ stop being subject to a rule his opponent is ⛔ still subject to?"* ⛔ If ⛔ YES, the option's ⛔ PRESENCE is ⛔ floored and only its ⛔ COST is exposed.**
- ⛔ **⛔ THE ⛔ ASYMMETRY IS THE ⛔ WHOLE HARM, AND IT MUST BE ⛔ NAMED WHEREVER IT IS FOUND: ⛔ a ⛔ CLIENT-SIDE visual that vanishes while the ⛔ SERVER-SIDE penalty persists means the ⛔ low-settings player gets ⛔ SIGHT ⛔ AND ⛔ KEEPS THE ENEMY'S ⛔ BLINDNESS.** ⛔ **⛔ A symmetric loss (⛔ both players see worse) is a ⛔ TRADEOFF; ⛔ an asymmetric one is an ⛔ EXPLOIT. ⛔ SAY WHICH.**
- ⛔ **⛔ THE ⛔ FLOOR IS ⛔ NOT A LEVER, AND THE ⛔ COUNT MUST NOT MOVE: ⛔ a ⛔ LEVER is a control the ⛔ PLAYER MOVES; ⛔ a ⛔ FLOOR is one he ⛔ CANNOT. ⛔ Adding a floor ⛔ NEVER increments `GFX-§8`'s Tier D.**
- ⛔ **⛔ WHERE A FLOOR IS ⛔ ENFORCED: ⛔ IN THE ⛔ FEATURE'S OWN CODE, ⛔ AT THE MOMENT THE FEATURE IS ⛔ LIVE — ⛔ never in the settings facade, ⛔ never by ⛔ hiding a row from the menu, ⛔ never by ⛔ clamping the group.** ⛔ **⛔ GROUNDS: ⛔ clamping the ⛔ Shadows group to ⛔ protect fog would ⛔ take the ⛔ cheap-PC player's ⛔ shadow performance away ⛔ for the ⛔ 99% of the match with ⛔ no fog in it — ⛔ paying for integrity with ⛔ exactly the population `GFX-§8` was written for.**
- ⛔ **⛔ AND THE ⛔ HONEST DISCLOSURE OBLIGATION: ⛔ when a floor lands, ⛔ EVERY MENU STRING THAT DESCRIBED THE ⛔ OLD BEHAVIOUR IS ⛔ FALSE AND IS ⛔ RE-WORDED IN THE ⛔ SAME COMMIT** (`SC-§94` pointed at the player — ⛔ a menu that contradicts the game teaches him the menu lies, ⛔ which is the ⛔ exact failure `GFX-§7`'s learnability clause exists to prevent).
- ⚠️⛔ **⛔ WHAT THIS DOES ⛔ NOT SAY: it does ⛔ NOT ban a setting from ⛔ touching a gameplay-visible system. ⛔ View distance changes what you can ⛔ SEE and is ⛔ RIGHTLY scalable — ⛔ because the game ⛔ never intended to hide anything at that distance. ⛔ THE DISCRIMINATOR IS ⛔ INTENT-TO-HIDE, ⛔ not visibility.** ⛔ **⛔ A row that cites this section ⛔ states which side of that line its subject falls on ⛔ and why.**
- ⛔ **⛔ THE ⛔ STANDING CENSUS THIS BUYS, ⛔ BOARDED RATHER THAN REMEMBERED: ⛔ the fog was found by ⛔ HIM, ⛔ not by us ⇒ ⛔ there may be ⛔ others (⛔ candidates ⛔ NOT findings: ⛔ the `WITCH-§` invisibility VFX · ⛔ the war-map reveal · ⛔ ranged-unit tells · ⛔ hit flashes · ⛔ the `NS_` spell telegraphs a player ⛔ dodges). ⛔ ⭐ `TASK-1146` cl. 5 ⛔ opens that list; ⛔ it does ⛔ not close it.**

### `FOG-§12.5b` 🚨⛔⛔⛔⭐⭐⭐ **ACTUATION — ⛔ THE ⛔ SECOND AXIS OF A MEASUREMENT, ⛔ AND THE ⛔ ONE I ⛔ FORGOT TO PIN. ⛔ I PINNED ⛔ WHERE THE CAMERA STANDS ⛔ CHARACTER-FOR-CHARACTER AND ⛔ LEFT ⛔ HOW THE VALUE ARRIVED ⛔ ENTIRELY UNSPECIFIED — AND ⛔ THAT GAP IS ⛔ LARGER THAN THE ⛔ ACCEPTANCE BAND IT FEEDS.** (written 2026-09-08 by the manager, ⛔ on ⭐ `TASK-1167` rev-2's ⛔ routed lead + ⭐ `TASK-1172` §3's own numbers · ⛔ marker `FOG-12-5b-ACTUATION`)

1. 🚨⛔⛔⭐⭐⭐ **CLAUSE 1 — ⛔ THE RULE, ⛔ AND IT IS ⛔ DELIBERATELY WRITTEN TO ⛔ BIND ⛔ WHICHEVER WAY THE DIAGNOSIS LANDS, ⛔ BECAUSE THE DIAGNOSIS IS ⛔ RUNNING RIGHT NOW AND I ⛔ MAY NOT PRE-JUDGE IT (⭐ `SC-§101`).**
   - ✅ **⛔ **THE ⛔ ACCEPTANCE NUMBER IS ⛔ PRODUCED BY THE ⛔ ACTUATION THE ⛔ PLAYER EXPERIENCES.** ⛔ FOR ANY ASSET-BORNE VALUE THAT IS: ⛔ SAVED CDO ⇒ ⛔ FRESH CONSTRUCTION ⇒ ⛔ WARMUP ⇒ ⛔ CAPTURE. ⛔ `ACT=ship`.**
   - ⛔ **⛔ AN ⛔ IN-PLACE DRIVE (`ACT=in-place`) IS A ⛔ RANKING INSTRUMENT AND ⛔ NOTHING MORE. ⛔ IT MAY ⛔ ORDER CANDIDATES, ⛔ FIND A DIRECTION, ⛔ ESTABLISH A NOISE FLOOR, ⛔ PROVE A CHANNEL LIVE. ⛔ IT MAY ⛔ NEVER PRODUCE THE NUMBER A ⛔ GATE IS EVALUATED AGAINST, ⛔ NOR THE NUMBER A ⛔ COMMIT MESSAGE QUOTES.**
   - 🚨 **⛔ THE ⛔ CONTAMINATION CLAUSE, ⛔ WHICH IS THE ⛔ ACTUAL TEETH AND THE ⛔ ONLY PART THAT WOULD HAVE ⛔ CAUGHT THIS: ⛔ A ⛔ SHIP-PATH CAPTURE TAKEN IN A ⛔ PROCESS THAT ⛔ EARLIER DROVE THE SAME PARAMETER ⛔ IN PLACE IS ⛔ NOT A CLEAN `ACT=ship` NUMBER. ⛔ ⭐ `TASK-1172`'s TWO *"independent"* SHIP-PATH RUNS ⛔ AGREED TO `ΔB/G 0.0001` — ⛔ AND BOTH FOLLOWED A ⛔ 14-POINT IN-PLACE SWEEP IN THE ⛔ SAME EDITOR PROCESS. ⇒ ⛔ **⛔ REPLICATION ⛔ INSIDE ONE PROCESS IS ⛔ NOT REPLICATION; ⛔ IT CAN ⛔ ONLY MEASURE THE ⛔ STABILITY OF A ⛔ CONTAMINATION.** ⛔ AN ACCEPTANCE FIGURE IS ⛔ REPLICATED ⛔ ACROSS A ⛔ PROCESS BOUNDARY: ⛔ EDITOR ⛔ CLOSED, ⛔ REOPENED, ⛔ NOTHING DRIVEN, ⛔ MEASURE.**
   - ⚖️ **⛔ WHY THIS BINDS ⛔ EITHER WAY, ⛔ STATED SO NO DIAGNOSIS CAN ⛔ MOOT IT: ⛔ (i) if the in-place rig reads ⛔ HIGH, ⛔ its numbers were never acceptance-grade ⇒ ⛔ rule holds · ⛔ (ii) if the ⛔ FRESH SPAWN reads ⛔ LOW, ⛔ then the ⛔ LOW number is what the ⛔ PLAYER'S MACHINE PRODUCES ⇒ ⛔ rule holds, ⛔ and the low number is the ⛔ true one · ⛔ (iii) if the cause is ⛔ NEITHER (⛔ exposure history, ⛔ a scatter seed, ⛔ time-of-session) ⇒ ⛔ the rule ⛔ still selects the ⛔ player-facing configuration and ⛔ costs one editor restart. ⛔ **⛔ THERE IS ⛔ NO OUTCOME IN WHICH IT IS ⛔ WRONG, ⛔ WHICH IS THE ⛔ ONLY REASON I MAY WRITE IT ⛔ BEFORE THE ANSWER.**

3. 🚨⛔⛔⭐⭐⭐ **CLAUSE 3 — ⛔ THE ⛔ TIE-BREAK, ⛔ WRITTEN NOW SO IT IS ⛔ NOT DECIDED BY WHOEVER SPEAKS LAST. ⛔ WHEN TWO ROWS REPORT ⛔ DIFFERENT NUMBERS FOR THE ⛔ SAME NOMINAL STATE:**

### `FOG-§12.5c` 🚨⛔⛔⛔⭐⭐⭐ **THE ⛔ WINDOW — ⛔ THE ⛔ THIRD AXIS, ⛔ THE ⛔ RE-PIN, ⛔ AND THE ⛔ REASON A ⛔ SINGLE FRAME MAY ⛔ NEVER AGAIN DECIDE THIS BAND.** (pinned 2026-09-09 by the manager, on ⭐ `TASK-1172` §REV-2's routed `SC-§82` item — ⛔ the artist ⛔ MEASURED BOTH BANDS AND ⛔ DELIBERATELY CHANGED NEITHER · ⛔ marker `FOG-12-5c-WINDOW`)

## ⚖️ THE VERIFICATION LANE — Aura Play-In-Editor evidence behind a `verified` gate (2026-09-13) — namespace **`VER-§`**

Written 2026-09-13 by the manager under `TASK-1226` (plan `look-into-a-new-moonlit-kernighan.md` Part B item 10; source doc `Docs/Aura AI for Unreal — Integration Plan.md` §4 Phase 3 steps 4–7 + §6 draft body; ⛔ the plan's *"Corrections to the doc"* table overrides the doc where they differ). Sections cite as `VER-§N`, never bare `§N`. Marker `VER-LANE-2026-09-13`. ⛔ Board rows CITE this section; no row's `spec:` restates it.

**Why it exists, in one sentence:** the board header records that a `qa-passed` is a TEXT-LEVEL verification — `qa-reviewer` holds no engine surface and sits BEFORE the compile — so until now no agent could press a key, watch a widget, or see PIE, and the first runtime observation of any change was 🧑 Jonathan's own playtest. Aura's Verification Agent (tryaura.dev) drives PIE, simulates input, reads live actor + UMG state, and screenshots — exposed to Claude Code as MCP tools. This lane is the seventh agent, `playtest-verifier`, that turns those tools into an evidence-backed runtime verdict and the new `verified` gate between `built` and `integrating`.

### VER-§0. PURPOSE — WHAT A `VERIFIED` IS, AND ⛔ WHAT IT IS NOT
1. **The lane.** After a code row is `qa-passed` (text) and `built` (binaries exist), and only if its spec names a runtime-observable acceptance criterion, `playtest-verifier` maps each acceptance line to an observable, drives one PIE run through Aura's tools, and writes `.claude/pipeline/qa/TASK-###-verify.md` with `Verdict: VERIFIED | VERIFY-FAILED | UNOBSERVABLE`. Blueprint/asset-only rows enter from `qa-passed` directly (there is nothing to compile). The routing (5a compile → 5b verify → 5c commit) lives in `CLAUDE.md`; this section is the law those steps cite.
2. **A `VERIFIED` IS:** *"the engine, driven this way, did this, and here is the frame / the quoted widget value / the log line that shows it."* It is evidence gathered BEFORE 🧑 Jonathan's playtest so that his time is spent on judgment, not on discovering that a button does nothing.
3. **⛔ A `VERIFIED` IS NOT:** ⛔ not his playtest, ⛔ not a substitute for it, ⛔ not a `qa-passed` (the two verdicts are kept SEPARATE and both stay honest — *"the text says what it should"* vs *"the engine did what it should"*), ⛔ not a claim about anything the run did not observe, and ⛔ not a claim about taste (`SHIP-§8b(7)`: his eye wins). **`FR-§` ground truth stays:** a footage-review finding from HIS recording outranks a `VERIFIED` on the same behaviour — the verifier drove a scripted input; he played the game.
4. **The pixel-proof doctrine is inherited whole** (`FR-§3`, `SC-§20`): observations with evidence paths and quoted values, never conclusions; mechanism lines are HYPOTHESIS; a time-varying claim states its observation window in seconds (`SC-§115`).
5. **Until `VER-§6` is discharged the whole lane is ADVISORY** — see that section before treating any verdict as a gate.

### VER-§1. REPORT SHAPE — `.claude/pipeline/qa/TASK-###-verify.md`
1. **Line 1 is the verdict, byte-literal:** `Verdict: VERIFIED` · `Verdict: VERIFY-FAILED` · `Verdict: UNOBSERVABLE` — nothing precedes it (the H1 `# Verification — TASK-###` is line 2), so `head -1` of any report IS its verdict. ~~During the `VER-§6` pilot the line carries the suffix ` (advisory — VER-§6 pilot)`.~~ (struck 2026-09-14, `TASK-1273`, on 🧑 his *"binding"* ruling — `VER-§6` cl. 5: from that date line 1 carries NO suffix, the template at `.claude/agents/playtest-verifier.md:80` emits none, and the five pilot reports that still carry it are historical records, not defective; a post-amendment report carrying the suffix is measured as if it did not — the verdict word alone governs.)
2. **Line 3+:** `Editor/Aura state:` (connected y/n, map, PIE mode, editor instance identified by command line per `SC-§118`, attempts used of 3, wall time, credit if visible). **The log file is NAMED, never defaulted (AMENDED 2026-09-14, `TASK-1273` (c); source `qa/TASK-780-verify.md` §Not examined + `AURA-PHASE0.md` §Pilot lane facts, `TASK-1230` R-LANE):** whenever the report quotes an editor log line it names the file it read, chosen by matching that file's line-1 `Log file open` timestamp to the driven instance's creation time (the PID from the `SC-§118` command-line identification) — ⛔ never by `get_unreal_output_logs`'s default: after the Probe 5 relaunch the tool served the PREVIOUS instance's `Saved/Logs/GitClaudeUnrealTest_2.log` (`log_source=editor-cached`) while the live PID 6136 was writing the base-name file, and a line from the wrong instance reads as a finding about this run. A log line quoted from an unnamed file is an empty cell under cl. 3.
3. **`## Acceptance lines → observations`** — one row per acceptance line of the task, in board order, columns exactly: `| # | acceptance line | observable chosen | observed (quoted values, evidence path) | pass/fail/unobs |` (AMENDED 2026-09-13, manager ruling R14, from `qa/TASK-1261-report.md` NIT-2 — the literal is now the shipped template header at `.claude/agents/playtest-verifier.md:84`, character for character; the two parentheticals the old literal carried were cell RULES, not column names, and live in the next sentence). **Cell rules:** the `acceptance line` cell is the row's acceptance text quoted VERBATIM, never paraphrased · the `observed` cell carries the PIE time as `t=<MM>m<SS>s` whenever the frame's time is known (the same value as `VER-§4` cl. 2's `-t…`) · the last cell is exactly one of `pass` / `fail` / `unobs`. ⛔ An acceptance line missing from this table is a defective report, not an implicit pass. ⛔ *"works"*, *"looks right"*, *"as expected"* are banned cell contents — a cell without a quoted value or an evidence path is empty. ~~Retired literal (2026-09-13 morning): `| # | acceptance line (quoted verbatim from the row) | observable chosen | observed (quoted values, evidence path, t=) | pass / fail / unobs |`~~ — kept struck so a reader who remembers it finds its correction; ⛔ a report carrying the retired header is measured against the current one.
4. **`## Evidence (promoted)`** — the `VER-§4` paths, one per line, each with a one-line dense pixel description (the shape the manager already consumes from `FR-§4`). **`## Hypotheses (not verdicts)`** — mechanism guesses, labelled. **`## Not examined / limitations this run`** — the lines marked `unobs`, the inputs Aura could not simulate, the window that was too short, anything the ≤3-attempt budget left untried.
5. **Verdict derivation, mechanical:** any `fail` ⇒ `VERIFY-FAILED` · no `fail` and ≥1 `pass` ⇒ `VERIFIED` (the `unobs` lines are listed under Not examined and the row gets `verify: partial (n/m observable)` when n<m) · no `fail` and no `pass` ⇒ `UNOBSERVABLE` (`VER-§5`). ⛔ A verifier that has never returned `VERIFY-FAILED` on a deliberately broken input is not a gate (plan Verification row 5) — the pilot must exhibit one. **Exhibited: Probe 5, `d3ade81` (`qa/TASK-1230-verify.md`; `TASK-1230` R-MATCH row P5). A deliberate break is proven by HASH, both ways (AMENDED 2026-09-14, `TASK-1273` (e); `SC-§68`):** the broken working-tree state is shown ARMED and then REVERTED by oid-vs-sha256 against the committed blob (`handoffs/TASK-1230-buildmaster.md` §6–§7), ⛔ never by size — Probe 5's mutated and committed `DT_Cards.uasset` were BOTH 46510 B, so a size check would have read the break as "unchanged" before the run and could not have told reverted from still-broken after it. A future exhibit that cannot quote the two hashes has not proven its break existed.
6. **Attempts:** ≤3 per task; every attempt's evidence is kept and named (`VER-§4` `-a<N>`), never only the cleanest. An `Aura not connected` / editor-down condition is an OUTAGE (`🚧`, no verdict line), ⛔ never an `UNOBSERVABLE` and never a fabricated run.

### VER-§2. SERIALIZATION — ⛔ ONE VERIFICATION AT A TIME, AND ⛔ NEVER BESIDE A BUILD OR AN IMPORT
1. **Exactly one Aura verification is live across the whole pipeline at any moment.** The verifier drives the editor; two drivers on one editor is the same defect as two compile gates on one module (`THE QUIET-MODULE LAW`).
2. **⛔ Never concurrent with:** a build-master compile gate (the editor must be down or relaunching — there is nothing to verify against), a build-master assemble (any row reading `integrating`), or an art-director import (the editor's asset state is mid-mutation). **The verifier's own pre-flight:** read the board; if ANY row reads `integrating`, or the orchestrator has announced a compile gate, ⛔ stop and post `🚧` — do not start. **The orchestrator's duty (where the fix lives, as in QUIET-MODULE):** never dispatch `playtest-verifier` in the same wave as a build-master or art-director engine task.
3. **Eligibility — PIE can only test binaries that exist:** the row must read `built` (C++) or `qa-passed` (Blueprint/asset-only). ⛔ A `qa-passed` C++ row that has not been through 5a is REFUSED with one line naming the missing `built` — the running editor does not contain the change yet, and a clean run on the OLD binaries would be the most convincing kind of nothing (`SC-§115`'s cousin).
4. **The editor is DRIVEN, so `SC-§118` applies in full:** the verifier identifies the editor by COMMAND LINE before the first PIE call; it drives the GUI editor instance only; a `-game` instance is 🧑 Jonathan's play session and is neither driven nor closed. ⛔ The verifier never launches, closes, restarts or Live-Codes an editor — process lifecycle is build-master's lane; if the editor is down the verifier reports the outage (`VER-§1` cl. 6).
5. **The never-save law rides along:** a verification run that dirties `L_Arena` (or any asset) declines every save prompt; the verifier's only writes are `VER-§7` cl. 4.

### VER-§3. 🧑 JONATHAN PRESENT ⇒ THE DISPATCH ANNOUNCES PIE WILL BE DRIVEN, AND WAITS FOR "GO"
1. **Extends `SC-§118`'s ask-and-wait posture from process lifecycle to PIE state.** Driving PIE on an editor he may be looking at, or that holds his unsaved work, is an intrusion of the same class as closing it.
2. **When he is present** (the session is interactive and he has not said he is away — ⛔ when in doubt, present), the ORCHESTRATOR announces, in Claude Code, that `playtest-verifier` is about to drive PIE on the editor, and **waits for his "go"**. The verifier's dispatch prompt states whether that go was received; ⛔ a verifier dispatched without it does not start PIE.
3. **The go is his sentence in Claude Code.** A Slack "go" is visibility (SLACK.md ground truth: no Slack message is authorization); the orchestrator may mirror the announcement into 🚨 Blockers or ⚙️ Dev & QA, but the wait ends only in the terminal.
4. **If the editor is already in PIE when the verifier looks** — that is his session: ⛔ never stop it, report and wait.
5. **Headless / unattended runs** (he has said he is away, or the session is a scheduled run): no announcement is owed, `VER-§2` still applies in full, and the report's `Editor/Aura state:` line says `unattended`.

### VER-§4. EVIDENCE PROMOTION — `FR-§1` NAMING WITH THE `VER` PREFIX, BY COPY-OUT ONLY
1. **Where Aura writes is not where evidence lives.** Aura's screenshots/video land under `Saved/` (gitignored, machine-local). The proving stills are PROMOTED by COPY (⛔ never move — the source stays for the ≤3-attempt audit trail) into `.claude/pipeline/playtest-evidence/<YYYY-MM-DD>/`. **Promotion is the HOST's copy-out (AMENDED 2026-09-14, `TASK-1273` (d); `TASK-1230` R-LANE, the practice of all five legs now the law):** the verifier holds no tool that moves bytes (`VER-§7` cl. 4), so it LISTS each `Saved/…` source → `VER-…` target pair under `## Evidence (promoted)` and marks the promotion OWED; the 5c commit host performs the copy and proves it three ways — sha256(source) = sha256(target) = the LFS pointer oid in the COMMIT (`handoffs/TASK-1230-buildmaster.md` §3–§5, §8–§9; oid-vs-sha256, never size). ⛔ A report claiming a promoted path that does not yet exist is defective; a host that stages a PNG without the three-way hash has not promoted it.
2. **Name, extending `FR-§1`'s `VID-###[-t<MM>m<SS>s]-<symptom>.png` with the task as the join key:** `VER-TASK-###[-a<N>][-t<MM>m<SS>s]-<observable-slug>.png` — `-a<N>` = attempt index (omit when only one attempt exists), `-t…` = PIE time of the frame when known, `<observable-slug>` = the acceptance-table observable in kebab-case, ⛔ never the word "pass"/"fail". Manual screenshots and `handoffs/TASK-###-…` stills keep their existing shapes (`FR-§1` evidence row) — the `VER` prefix is reserved for frames the verifier's run produced.
3. **⛔ Video is never promoted** (`FR-§0` cl. 2 — `*.mp4` is an LFS pattern and videos never enter git). A video path may be QUOTED in the report as `Saved/…` (machine-local, non-committed, may be gone tomorrow); the still that proves the line is the evidence.
4. **`FR-§6` applies unchanged:** promoted PNGs are an LFS pattern and need a NAMED evidence host row — the trailing doc-host carries the `TASK-###-verify.md` and ⛔ cannot carry the PNGs. Whoever boards the commit boards the host.
5. **Promote what proves, not everything:** one still per observed acceptance line is the norm; the rest stays in `Saved/`.

### VER-§5. `UNOBSERVABLE` — THE HONEST ANSWER, ⛔ NEVER A PASS
1. **Meaning.** Aura's own docs: *"Changes with no runtime signal… can't be meaningfully verified."* A pure-data row (a DataTable value, a config default), an editor-only row, a law/doc row, a refactor with no behavioural claim — these have no observable and get `UNOBSERVABLE`, with the reason per line in the table (`unobs` + why). ⛔ The verifier does not invent a proxy to avoid the word (the `FR-§5` colour-census lesson: a proxy that correlates is still not the claim).
2. **Board semantics.** The row's `status:` DOES NOT MOVE — it stays `built` (C++) or `qa-passed` (asset-only); the verifier appends `verify: unobservable` to its own row (WRITE DISCIPLINE rule 1 — status line only). The report still lands with `Verdict: UNOBSERVABLE` on line 1. Routing then proceeds to 5c exactly as a row with no runtime criterion would; the commit host's handoff names the `unobservable` so it is never read downstream as `verified`.
3. **⛔ It is never a pass, and it is never an outage.** `UNOBSERVABLE` = *the row has nothing PIE can see*. `Aura down` / `editor down` / `tool not granted` = `🚧` blocked, no verdict (`VER-§1` cl. 6). *"Absent"* and *"empty"* are different measurements (`FR-§5`, `SC-§39`) — a report that blurs them is defective.
4. **Partial rows** (some lines observed, some not) are NOT `UNOBSERVABLE` — `VER-§1` cl. 5 governs, and the `verify: partial (n/m observable)` note goes on the row.
5. **The UMG-button blind spot (ADDED 2026-09-14, `TASK-1273` (b); sources `qa/TASK-671-verify.md`, `qa/TASK-787-verify.md`, `TASK-1230` R-LANE / R-MATCH row N3).** Any flow gated on a UMG button click is `UNOBSERVABLE` BY CONSTRUCTION until a verifier-actuable route exists (`TASK-1274`, optional, 🧑 his call): on `L_MainMenu` no input mapping context is applied (`applied_mapping_contexts: []`), `simulate_key_press` is delivered to the player controller and not to Slate (8× Tab → `binding_found: false`, no node `focused: true`), and `ui_perform`'s three click shapes never fire `OnClicked` (`down handled=true / up handled=false`) — these three are NAMED DEAD ENDS, ⛔ not re-traced by any later dispatch. The verifier says so in ONE attempt (N3's shape: ≈56 s of PIE, ≈12 min wall) and spends no more of its budget; the row then routes per cl. 2. Flows affected today: deck builder, sandbox, settings, login, multiplayer. ⛔ Never a false `VERIFIED` by proxy (cl. 1) — and ⛔ never a `VERIFY-FAILED` either: a button the verifier cannot press is not a button that does not work. What DOES reach our code: `inject_input_action` on our Enhanced Input actions (`IA_Move`, `IA_Card1`, `IA_DiscardAll` all reached `IMC_Hero` on N1/N2/N4), so Route B (`load_level L_Arena` direct, vs-bot) is the working substitute for every in-match observable.

### VER-§7. TOOL-GRANT LAW — WHAT THE VERIFIER HOLDS, AND ⛔ WHAT NO AGENT MAY BE HANDED
1. **⛔⛔ NEVER `mcp__unreal_editor__*` wholesale** — in any `permissions.allow`, in any agent `tools:` line, in any dispatch. `unreal_editor` bundles the PIE / verify / screenshot tools with C++ authoring, Live Coding compile and shell tools; a wholesale grant hands compilation to every agent and breaks the `QUIET-MODULE` law, the never-Live-Coding law and QA's read-only-by-design posture in one line.
2. **Enumerated from the census, or not at all.** The PIE / verify / screenshot tool names come ONLY from `handoffs/AURA-MCP-CENSUS.md` (the orchestrator's `/mcp` census — Aura's docs enumerate none of them). A name absent from the current census is not grantable; when Aura updates, the census is re-run before any grant is trusted. The verifier's `tools:` line is that enumeration plus `Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit`, the ENUMERATED `unreal_inspector` read set (cl. 3), and the two Slack tools — ⛔ a draft carrying a placeholder is never committed. **The sequence runner's own whitelist is a GRANT SURFACE (AMENDED 2026-09-14, `TASK-1273` (f) — R-N1's deferred note lands here; sources `qa/TASK-787-verify.md`, `qa/TASK-780-verify.md` §Not examined, census §5 "PIE-world mutation (staging)", `handoffs/TASK-1224-programmer.md` §tools-line census):** on N1 and N4 the verifier staged a tower through `pie_scene_edit spawn_actor` — a name on neither its `tools:` line nor `permissions.allow` — reached as a STEP inside `run_verification_sequence`, whose step vocabulary the harness's grant check does not see. MEASURED FACT, not a defect finding and ⛔ not a grant: the action is `SC-§101`'s — the census (`handoffs/AURA-MCP-CENSUS.md`) is re-run with the runner's step vocabulary enumerated as its own section before any further grant is trusted, and cl. 1's wholesale ban is read to cover names reachable THROUGH a granted tool. A verifier that reaches a census §5 name through the runner reports it in `## Not examined / limitations`, as N1 and N4 did.
3. **`mcp__unreal_inspector__*` — ⛔ NOT wholesale either (AMENDED 2026-09-13, manager ruling R10, from the census §2a).** The server's NAME said read-only; the census MEASURED 13 non-read tools inside it — engine lifecycle (`launch_unreal_project`, `recompile_unreal_project`, `shutdown_headless`, `cancel_operation`), generation (`generate_images`, `generate_model_from_image`, `generate_model_from_text`, `edit_images`, `derive_normal_map`, `rig_model_from_mesh`, `get_recent_generated_images`) and plan bookkeeping (`create_or_edit_plan`, `lock_plan_layer`). `recompile_unreal_project` is a COMPILE PATH; cl. 1's reason — *a wildcard hands compilation to every agent, and a body law is not a harness* — does not change with the server's name, and the seven generation tools are cl. 5's mutating agents under another door (spending Aura credit on a mis-call). ⇒ **The inspector grant is the ENUMERATED read set — census §2 minus §2a = 49 names, one per entry** — in `permissions.allow` and in the `qa-reviewer` + `playtest-verifier` `tools:` lines alike (`SC-§71b`: QA may INSPECT a Blueprint graph or the editor log to check a declaration; its no-mutation posture is unchanged). The 13 are granted to no pipeline agent; ⛔ a `mcp__unreal_inspector__*` token anywhere is cl. 1's class of defect. ~~Retired text (2026-09-13 morning): "`mcp__unreal_inspector__*` (read-only) MAY be granted wholesale — to the verifier and to `qa-reviewer`"~~ — kept struck so a reader who remembers it finds its correction instead of re-deriving the grant. 📌 LEAD, not law (`SC-§101`): a `permissions.deny` entry for the four lifecycle names would make the harness REFUSE rather than prompt; that a deny honours an MCP name is unmeasured here, so it rides the first row that needs it.
4. **What the verifier is NOT, enumerated:** it holds ⛔ no `Bash`, ⛔ no `unreal-mcp` (:8000 — actor/scene mutation is build-master's and art-director's surface), ⛔ no `blender`, ⛔ no Git; it never calls an editor LIFECYCLE tool (launch / close / restart / Live Coding), a COMPILE tool, or an AUTHORING tool (asset, Blueprint, C++ or level mutation) — even if such a name were mis-granted, calling it is a failed task. **Its only legal writes are:** its own `TASK-###-verify.md`, its own row's `status:` line (+ the `verify:` note), ~~and the `VER-§4` copy-out~~ (struck 2026-09-14, `TASK-1273` (d): the verifier holds no tool that moves bytes — it LISTS the copy-out and the 5c host performs it, `VER-§4` cl. 1). A verifier diff in any other file is a failed task (the `FR-§0` cl. 3 diagnose-only model).
5. **Aura's own mutating agents** (Blueprint, Material, Niagara, mesh generation, C++) are ⛔ NOT part of this lane and are granted to no pipeline agent. Aura mesh output never writes `Content/` — it re-enters through `Tools/ArtPipeline` Stage 2 (`TL-§`). Aura's Filesystem Sandbox is the undo for Aura-driven asset edits made in Aura's own chat, not a licence for agents to make them.
6. **The `Saved/.Aura/` folder** is machine-local and NEVER staged; its two files are regenerated from the canonical `Docs/AuraIndexIgnore.txt` + `Docs/AuraProjectMemory.md` by `Tools/aura_sync.ps1` (the artefact table above). Editing the `Saved/` copies by hand is the `FOG-§12.4c` shape — the next sync overwrites it and nothing errors.
7. ⚠️⭐⭐ **THE `unreal-mcp` BRIDGE — ⛔ ITS ARGUMENT SHAPE AND ⛔ WHAT THE GRANT ACTUALLY LICENSES (added 2026-09-18 by the manager, on `TASK-1298`'s 5a leg · ⛔ the wrong shape was the ⛔ ORCHESTRATOR'S, quoted in a dispatch, and it ⛔ cost the host a ⛔ failed call).**
   - ⛔⛔ **THE SHAPE, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT COSTS A CALL: `mcp__unreal-mcp__call_tool` TAKES ⛔ `toolset_name` ⛔ AND `tool_name` AS ⛔ TWO SEPARATE ARGUMENTS.** ⇒ ✅ `toolset_name = "BlueprintTools"`, `tool_name = "compile_blueprint"`. ⛔ **THE ⛔ FULLY-QUALIFIED ⛔ SINGLE-STRING FORM — `editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools.compile_blueprint` — RETURNS ⛔ `Tool not found`.** ⛔ **Write the two fields; ⛔ never the dotted path.**
   - ✅ **WHAT THE GRANT ⛔ LICENSES, ⛔ MEASURED OPEN 2026-09-18 (⛔ no `[Modify Shared Resources]` denial and ⛔ no permission prompt on ⛔ four calls): ⛔ THESE ⛔ ENUMERATED read/compile/save calls ⛔ through that bridge** — `BlueprintTools.compile_blueprint` (⛔ properties: `blueprint`, `warnings_as_errors` — ⛔ **and ⛔ NOTHING ELSE; a sweep of ⛔ all 53 `BlueprintTools` entries for `save|dirty|flush|persist|to disk` returned ⛔ ZERO hits**) · `AssetTools.save_assets` (`asset_paths` — ⛔ **no force flag**) · `AssetTools.is_dirty`.
   - ⛔⛔ **WHAT IT DOES ⛔ NOT LICENSE, ⛔ SAID IN FULL BECAUSE A ⛔ MEASURED GRANT IS ⛔ EXACTLY WHAT GETS OVER-READ:** ⛔ the ⛔ UNLISTED `mcp__unreal_editor__*` tools — ⛔ **cl. 1 and cl. 3 and ruling R10 ⛔ STAND UNTOUCHED** · ⛔ any ⛔ OTHER toolset · ⛔ any ⛔ MUTATING call those four never made · ⛔ and it is ⛔ **NOT a licence to ⛔ hunt for a tool that slips through** — ⛔ a refusal is ⛔ reported, ⛔ never routed around (`SC-§54` cl. 1).
   - 🚨⛔ **AND THE TRAP THAT LIVES ⛔ INSIDE THE GRANT: ⛔ `save_assets` RETURNS `true` WHEN IT WROTE ⛔ NOTHING** (⛔ a Blueprint compile does ⛔ not dirty the package) ⇒ ⛔ **an agent holding this grant may ⛔ NOT report a `.uasset` as saved on the strength of the return value. ⛔ Read ⛔ sha256 ⛔ AND byte count ⛔ AND mtime — ⛔ law ⭐ `SC-§125`.**

### VER-§8. 🚨⛔⛔⛔⭐⭐⭐ THE CAPABILITY CEILING IS DECLARED AT ⛔ BOARDING TIME, ⛔ NEVER DISCOVERED AT 5b — **A SLATE KEYPRESS IS ⛔ NOT VERIFIABLE BY THIS RIG, AND THAT IS NOW ⛔ MEASURED TWICE WITH A FIRING CONTROL PAIR** (added 2026-09-18 by the manager, on the `TASK-1286` → `TASK-1306` pair · marker `VER-8-DECLARE-THE-CEILING-AT-BOARDING`)

> ### ⛔⛔ **`VER-§5` cl. 5 TELLS THE ⛔ VERIFIER WHAT TO DO WHEN IT HITS THE CEILING. ⛔ THIS CLAUSE TELLS THE ⛔ MANAGER NOT TO WRITE A ROW THAT WALKS INTO IT — AND THE ⛔ TWO ARE NOT THE SAME DUTY. ⛔ A BLIND SPOT FOUND AT 5b HAS ALREADY COST A DISPATCH, A PIE SESSION AND A ROUND OF 🧑 HIS ATTENTION.**

1. ⛔⛔ **CLAUSE 1 — THE MEASURED CEILING, ⛔ AND IT IS MEASURED, ⛔ NOT INFERRED — ⛔ TWICE, ⛔ ON TWO SEPARATE PIE SESSIONS, ⛔ WITH A ⛔ DISCRIMINATING CONTROL PAIR BOTH TIMES.** `simulate_key_press` is ⛔ **delivered to the player controller / Enhanced Input and ⛔ NOT to Slate** — the tool's ⛔ own words: *"Key Tab was ⛔ delivered to the player controller."* ⛔ **THE CONTROL PAIR, which is what makes this a measurement rather than a complaint:** `Tab` (⛔ Slate's own `Next` key, ⛔ `binding_found: false`) moved focus ⛔ NOT AT ALL, while `Down` (⛔ `binding_found: true`, `IA_MenuDown`) ⛔ DID move it. ⇒ ⛔ **the injector works; ⛔ it works at a layer beneath the one Slate reads.** ⛔ **The second run (`TASK-1306`) re-took the control ⛔ STRONGER: one injected `Down` left `FocusedCardIndex` at `-1` ⛔ WHILE the builder root itself ⛔ demonstrably held Slate focus — so `SWidget::OnKeyDown` would have converted the key to navigation and moved something ⛔ had the key arrived at all.**
2. 🚨⛔⛔ **CLAUSE 2 — THE BOARDING RULE, ⛔ AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS SECTION: ⛔ ANY ROW WHOSE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS A ⛔ SLATE KEYPRESS OR A ⛔ UMG BUTTON CLICK IS ⛔ UNVERIFIABLE BY THE CURRENT RIG, ⛔ AND THE ROW SAYS SO ⛔ IN ITS OWN SPEC ⛔ BEFORE IT IS DISPATCHED.** ⛔ Not in the handoff, ⛔ not in the verify report, ⛔ not in the retrospective — ⛔ **in the spec, where the assignee and the gate both read it.** ⇒ ⛔ **discovering the ceiling at 5b is ⛔ a MANAGER defect, ⛔ not a verifier finding** (`SC-§123` cl. 8: the defect lives in the spec that named an entry route and required nobody to measure it).
   - ⭐⭐⛔ **THE `.uasset` TWIN, ⛔ ADDED 2026-09-18 (⭐ `SC-§125` cl. 3) — ⛔ IT IS THE ⛔ SAME DUTY ON A ⛔ DIFFERENT CEILING, AND IT BITES AT ⛔ 5a RATHER THAN 5b: ⛔ ANY ROW WHOSE DELIVERABLE IS A ⛔ COMPILED BLUEPRINT CARRIES A 🧑 ⛔ HUMAN KEYSTROKE.** ⛔ **A UE5 Blueprint compile does ⛔ NOT dirty the package ⇒ `AssetTools.save_assets` returns ⛔ `true` and ⛔ writes nothing ⇒ ⛔ the ⛔ hash-must-change discharge is ⛔ UNREACHABLE programmatically and the ⛔ BP editor's ⛔ Compile → `Ctrl+S` is the ⛔ only unconditional writer.** ⇒ ⛔ **the row ⛔ NAMES that keystroke as a ⛔ DECLARED COST ⛔ AT BOARDING — ⛔ not at 5a, ⛔ not in the handoff, ⛔ not after a host has already stopped.** ⛔ First application: ⭐ `TASK-1311` (2).
3. ✅⛔ **CLAUSE 3 — WHAT THE ROW MUST DO ⛔ INSTEAD, AND IT IS ⛔ THREE PARTS, ⛔ ALL WRITTEN IN ADVANCE.**
   - ⛔ **(a) SPLIT THE CRITERION AT THE CEILING.** Name the half a ⛔ STATE READ can settle (who holds focus · a `ui_snapshot` · a `FocusedCardIndex` read · a `.sav` hash) and the half it cannot. ⛔ **The state-read half is a ⛔ REAL acceptance line and it ⛔ discriminates: `TASK-1306` (5a) pre-decided that focus ⛔ still outside the builder would be a ⛔ `VERIFY-FAILED`, ⛔ not an `UNOBSERVABLE` — ⛔ because the instrument demonstrably works for ⛔ that reading.** ⇒ ⛔ **a ceiling on ⛔ one half is ⛔ never a licence to stop measuring the ⛔ other.**
   - 🧑 ⛔ **(b) SPEC 🧑 HIS ONE-SENTENCE HAND CHECK ⛔ IN ADVANCE, ⛔ VERBATIM, ⛔ WITH THE FALSE POSITIVES NAMED IN A PARENTHESIS.** ⛔ **THE SHAPE THAT WORKED, kept whole because the wording ⛔ IS the instrument:** ***"Open the deck builder, press `Down` once, then press `Enter` — does the deck total at the top go up by one? (An outline appearing, or the card's details panel opening, is a NO.)"*** ⛔ **The parenthesis is ⛔ LOAD-BEARING and ⛔ may not be trimmed** — Slate's own navigation draws an outline and `SButton`'s Accept path opens the details panel ⛔ with every line of our feature dead (`SC-§123` cl. 6). ⇒ ⛔ **ask for the effect ⛔ ONLY our code can produce.** ⛔ **The sentence is written ⛔ at boarding, ⛔ not improvised at 5b, ⛔ because that is when there is time to get the parenthesis right.**
   - ⛔ **(c) NAME THE ROUTING UP FRONT:** the row sits at `built` + `verify: unobservable — pending 🧑 his one sentence`, the ⛔ commit still proceeds per `VER-§5` cl. 2 (an `UNOBSERVABLE` ⛔ never blocks), and 🧑 his answer is recorded ⛔ verbatim ⛔ ALONGSIDE the verdict. ⛔ **The commit host does ⛔ NOT edit the verify report and does ⛔ NOT re-verdict it** — ⛔ the report is the ⛔ rig's testimony about ⛔ the rig, and 🧑 his sentence is a ⛔ different witness.
4. ⚖️⭐⭐ **CLAUSE 4 — THE SHAPE TO COPY, STATED ONCE SO IT TRAVELS: ⛔ THE RIG MEASURES THE HALF IT CAN; 🧑 HIS HANDS MEASURE THE HALF NO RIG ON THIS PROJECT CAN — ⛔ AND THE TWO ARE RECORDED ⛔ SIDE BY SIDE, ⛔ NEVER MERGED.** ⛔ **An `UNOBSERVABLE` + his confirmation is ⛔ NOT a `VERIFIED`** and is ⛔ never written as one; the row's status line carries ⛔ both, and the commit message carries ⛔ both. ⇒ ⛔ **what makes this honest is that a reader can still see ⛔ exactly which half the machine proved.**
5. ⛔ **CLAUSE 5 — THE CEILING IS ⛔ RE-MEASURED, ⛔ NOT ASSUMED FOREVER.** This clause describes ⛔ today's rig. ⛔ **A row may ⛔ not re-trace the named dead ends to "check"** (`VER-§5` cl. 5 forbids exactly that spend) — ⛔ but if Aura ships a Slate-level input tool, the census (`handoffs/AURA-MCP-CENSUS.md`) is ⛔ re-run and ⛔ this clause is amended ⛔ in place, ⛔ dated, ⛔ before any row relies on the new capability (`SC-§101`).
6. ⚖️ **CLAUSE 6 — KINSHIP, CHECKED BEFORE MINTING (`SC-§116` cl. 3).** `VER-§5` cl. 5 (the ⛔ UMG-button blind spot — ⛔ the ⛔ VERIFIER's duty at the ceiling; ⛔ this is the ⛔ MANAGER's duty ⛔ before it) · `VER-§5` cl. 1/3 (⛔ never a pass, ⛔ never an outage) · `SC-§123` cl. 5 (⛔ a declared-unmeasured premise the feature depends on is a ⛔ BLOCKER, ⛔ not a caveat) and cl. 6 (⛔ the look-alike question) · `SC-§101` (⛔ a prescribed remedy is a claim) · `DECK-§9` cl. 6 (⛔ the first worked example, end to end).
